content.body:
Its WWI tank heritage evident in the round-the-hull track and nestled hull gun, the Char.B1bis was nevertheless a sophisticated piece of equipment. The turret was exactly the same as used on the S35, while in the hull was mounted a 75mm howitzer style gun. Massive armor protected it from all directions, it was nearly impossible to kill with the regular or average AT guns. It had a number of drawbacks, such as the slow speed, poor communications, the usual French one-man turret, as well as an excessively complex transmission.
Surprisingly for a vehicle so comprehensively protected, the Char had an Achilles' heel in its vulnerable left engine grille (which most Germans didnt discover until after the BoF was over). The Germans converted a number of captured Chars to Flame Tanks (some were used against British paras at Arnheim). The Free French recaptured others and employed them again against the Germans at the very end of the war.
Control Variations: Extremely different control set. This is a very distinct vehicle. Driver zooms in on view slit with (numpad 0 or Ins key). No periscope, closing view slit armor blocks view completely.
Driver also controls Hull Main Gun (75mm) use the numpad . Or Del key to look through gunsight/zoom. No range adjustment on Hull Gun, gradations only. Elevation controlled from driver's position by I (increase gun elevation) and K (decrease gun elevation). Gun traverse adjusted by steering vehicle. Commander is in a cupola, cannot unbutton. View is through an armored viewslit (key O to open). No view elevation change. View traverse speed limited to turret traverse speed. Gunner controls 47mm gun in top turret. Gunner has a viewport BEHIND him (key O to open) and numpad 0 or Ins key to look/zoom.
Loader (position 4) has no weapon, but can see a gauge that shows the direction the top turret is pointing relative to vehicle body. Use numpad 0 or Ins key to zoom in on gauge.
Playing the Char is an adventure in itself. There are so many things to do, it is far more effective multi-crewed than any other vehicle. Because of its slow speed, you have a lot of time to familiarize yourself with the complicated control suite, quite different than other tanks although not too different for anyone familiar with French vehicles. The Hull 75mm is extremely inaccurate and has a slow Rate of fire (RoF) so dont rely on blasting your way through anything with that. As the driver, you must always be aware of that left grille. Knowledgeable German gunners in this game have had 4 years of practice where the real ones barely had 4 weeks ... its now standard to shoot first at the right track of the Char to cause the tank to turn and expose its radiator grille. Tracks are relatively easy to destroy and (if the Char is moving) shooting the right one will make it swing around to the right, exposing the vulnerable left radiator grille to the shooter.
When facing these clever fellows, your best response is simply ... stop. Unlike almost every other tank, stopping in a Char is a perfectly reasonable tactic ... your gun stability will improve and you can directly cope with any threats to your left side with the turret gun, while your armor shrugs off the hits.
Keep a close eye out for 88s though, they are a threat to you if you let them get close enough so spray them constantly with MG fire, you may get lucky and kill the gunner. Like all French tanks, make sure you dont accidentally open the gunner's port. On other tanks, this would leave a very small vulnerability in the mantlet; on French tanks it opens the a gaping port on the entire back of the turret leaving your turret members entirely exposed to even pistol fire.
content.brief: TYPE: Heavy AFV ARMAMENT: 75mm Hull gun 47mm Main (turret) gun 2 x 7.5mm LMG WEIGHT: 32000 kg SPEED (road): 28 km/h
content.title: Char.B1(bis)
